digest.component_or_area: Jira Reconciler Bridge - baseline advance and field direction arbitration
propositions: The reconciler baseline is advanced from the pass-START snapshot (last-fetched) rather than the last-synced value, causing it to lag rebar's own outbound push by exactly one pass.

A local status change made after an outbound push but before the next baseline advance is suppressed outbound (because local now equals the stale baseline) and then clobbered inbound, while other fields from the same window survive because they differ from the stale baseline.

The bug affects all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) because all share the local==baseline suppression guard, making the ABA exposure a class defect not a status-only regression.

Per-mutation success (keyed off actual client.update_issue completion, not pass exit code) must gate baseline advance, since soft-failed mutations (illegal-transition RuntimeError, 400 comment-fallback) do not land a sync and must not falsely advance the baseline.

Advancing the baseline must overlay confirmed outbound mutations onto the fetched snapshot before set_baseline writes it, restoring ADR 0026's definition of baseline as last-synced rather than last-fetched, while preserving inbound mirroring of genuine Jira-side edits for unchanged local values.
